title: Choose the jobs page's structure
question: Three ways to organise the owner's jobs page inside QuantumLab's look. Pick one, steer it, or re-roll.

options.label: The month's statement
options.lineage: a bank statement: pending items, dated lines, a running balance
options.thesis: The month reads as an account statement: every job a dated line, a running balance against the cap.
options.viewport: Header: month, cap gauge and billed-vs-metered line. Pending items (running, failed) pinned above dated settled lines; each line opens its receipt.
options.risk: A finance metaphor may underplay results: Open result must stay a first-class action on every line.

options.label: Budget strip and one-line rows
options.thesis: One line per job with only the essentials; everything else opens inline under its row.
options.viewport: A budget strip on top, status filter chips, then single-line rows: molecule, status, runtime vs prediction, charged of maximum, Open result.
options.risk: Closest to the category standard: clean but the least distinctive of the three.

options.label: Month timeline over a list
options.lineage: a run log drawn against the calendar
options.thesis: The month drawn on one axis: each job a bar on its day, the cumulative spend rising toward the cap.
options.viewport: Top third: the October axis with job bars and the spend line against the $8.80 cap. Below: a compact synced list.
options.risk: The chart can tip into the busy dashboard look you want to avoid; it must stay one quiet band.
